**Direct answer:** Global semiconductor sales hit a record in 2024. The first figure SIA announced was $627.6 billion, up 19.1% from $526.8 billion in 2023. WSTS later revised the year-end total to $630.5 billion, which works out to about 19.7% growth. The revised $630.5 billion is the best final figure. Forecasts and regional growth rates are different kinds of numbers and shouldn't be mixed with it.

**Claims and sources**

- SIA announced 2024 sales of $627.6B, up 19.1% from $526.8B in 2023 (Feb 2025).
  https://www.semiconductors.org/global-semiconductor-sales-increase-19-1-in-2024-double-digit-growth-projected-in-2025/

- A March 3, 2025 update on the same page says WSTS revised the 2024 year-end total to $630.5B. That page gives no revised growth rate. The ~19.7% is my calculation from the two totals.
  https://www.semiconductors.org/global-semiconductor-sales-increase-19-1-in-2024-double-digit-growth-projected-in-2025/

- The 2025 SIA Factbook uses $630.5B for 2024. The WSTS Autumn 2025 table is reported (via search summary) as showing $630,549M and 19.7% growth. I could not read that PDF, so treat the WSTS figure as secondary.
  https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025-SIA-Factbook-FINAL-1.pdf
  https://www.wsts.org/esraCMS/extension/media/f/WST/7310/WSTS_FC-Release-2025_11.pdf

- SIA's February 2026 announcement reportedly uses $630.5B as the 2024 baseline. It puts 2025 sales at $791.7B, up 25.6%. I saw this only in a search summary, not on the page itself.
  https://atreg.com/global-2025-semiconductor-sales-rise-by-25-6-percent-to-791-7-billion/

- Some outlets still cite the older $627.6B figure.
  https://venturebeat.com/business/global-chip-sales-rose-19-1-in-2024-and-will-hit-double-digit-growth-in-2025-thanks-to-ai-sia
  https://www.trendforce.com/news/2025/02/08/news-global-semiconductor-sales-hit-record-high-at-600b-in-2024-set-for-double-digit-growth-in-2025/

- The regional 2024 growth rates in SIA's release were: Americas +44.8%, China +18.3%, Asia Pacific/All Others +12.5%, Japan −0.4%, Europe −8.1%. These are regional rates, not the global one. They come from the original release, so they predate the revision to $630.5B.
  https://www.semiconductors.org/global-semiconductor-sales-increase-19-1-in-2024-double-digit-growth-projected-in-2025/

- Forecasts are separate from the 2024 result. The WSTS Spring 2025 forecast (June 2025) projected 11.2% growth in 2025, to $700.9B. It was later revised up, to $728B (15.4%) at mid-year and then to $772.2B (22.5%) in autumn. The 2025 actual reported by SIA was +25.6%. These forecast figures come from a search summary, and I did not read the WSTS releases themselves.
  https://www.wsts.org/esraCMS/extension/media/f/WST/7057/WSTS_FC-Release-2025_05.pdf
  https://www.wsts.org/esraCMS/extension/media/f/WST/7310/WSTS_FC-Release-2025_11.pdf

**How to tell them apart**
1. **Finalized annual figure:** a world total for a completed year, from SIA/WSTS data. Use the latest revised value, here $630.5B, and say which release it comes from.
2. **Forecast:** WSTS projections for a future year, such as 2025 or 2026. They change with each release, so name the release date.
3. **Regional growth rate:** a year-over-year change for one region. It isn't the global figure, and it is not additive. For example, the Americas' +44.8% sits beside Europe's −8.1% inside a global +19%.

**Caveats:** I used four retrievals and did not read the WSTS PDF directly, because it came back unreadable. The final-versus-preliminary status of $630.5B rests on SIA's update note and the Factbook. I found no later revision, but I can't rule one out. Regional figures for the revised total were not available to me.

Sources:
- [SIA release on 2024 sales](https://www.semiconductors.org/global-semiconductor-sales-increase-19-1-in-2024-double-digit-growth-projected-in-2025/)
- [2025 SIA Factbook](https://www.semiconductors.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/2025-SIA-Factbook-FINAL-1.pdf)
- [WSTS Autumn 2025 forecast](https://www.wsts.org/esraCMS/extension/media/f/WST/7310/WSTS_FC-Release-2025_11.pdf)
